description: Small serialized table whose rows pair a CP_270_* key with a TArray<FName> of image names. Both exported rows contain only NAME_None entries. No runtime consumer of the table or of the corresponding CharacterVariation identifier was found in the reconstructed C++.

ID.simple: Serialized row key. Both exported keys are CP_270_* names that also occur as CharacterVariation row IDs.
ID.technical: Native FName Id (exported as property ID; ImportKeyField=Id). The row key equals ID in both rows. CharacterVariationDataTable.Id_CharacterUniqueImage is also FName and has exactly ten non-None values: CP_270_00 is referenced by variation rows CP_270_00..04, and CP_270_10 by CP_270_10..14. No reconstructed C++ reads Id_CharacterUniqueImage or performs a CharacterUniqueImageDataTable lookup. The table name is absent from AGameDataTableManager::StartInitialLoading's loader-name array and from Tick's table-resolution/cache assignments, and no CharacterUniqueImageDataTables array exists. This is therefore a data-level association only, not a verified runtime join.

ImageFileName.simple: Serialized list of image asset names; in both exported rows it consists of sixteen None entries.
ImageFileName.technical: Native TArray<FName> (UPROPERTY at row +0x10). Each exported row serializes sixteen elements at indices 0-15, every one the NAME_None sentinel; this is an observed serialized length, not a fixed array bound or evidence of index semantics. The constructor is empty, so a default-constructed struct has an empty TArray. The reconstruction's type-registration table records the retail struct at 0x16cc740 and its layout checks assert Id at +0x8 and ImageFileName at +0x10. Exact-qualified searches find no game-side read of FGameDataTableRow_CharacterUniqueImage::ImageFileName, no FindRow/GetRows instantiation for this row type, and no typed manager array; unrelated structs also have fields named ImageFileName, so their consumers do not apply here. No texture loader, UI branch, condition, fallback, or slot-specific behavior can be attributed to this field from the reconstructed source.

notes: Export analysis: one asset/variant named CharacterUniqueImageDataTable has exactly two row keys, CP_270_00 and CP_270_10. Each row's ID equals its row key and each ImageFileName array has sixteen entries, all None/NAME_None. No numbered or locale-shard files for this table were found.

Data relationship: in the 437-row CharacterVariationDataTable, Id_CharacterUniqueImage is None in 427 rows and points to the two exported CharacterUniqueImage rows from ten records (five per target). CharacterDataTable.CP_270 lists those ten variation IDs. This is serialized referential data, not a traced lookup.

Runtime evidence: the exact table name has no occurrence in Source/, Plugins/, or Config/; the row type appears only in its own header/constructor, the reconstruction's retail type-registration table, and verification/layout tooling. AGameDataTableManager loads and resolves CharacterUniqueDataTable1..5 but not CharacterUniqueImageDataTable, has no CharacterUniqueImageDataTables cache, and never instantiates FindRow or GetRows for this row type. Id_CharacterUniqueImage is likewise declaration-only.

Array semantics: sixteen is only the serialized element count (indices 0-15). TArray is dynamically sized and the empty constructor supplies no default elements; None is the sentinel used for absent names. No consumer establishes ordering, an index meaning, units, or precedence.

Layout/provenance: DataTableStructTables.cpp records retail struct address 0x16cc740, and reconstruction layout checks assert offsets 0x8 for Id and 0x10 for ImageFileName. These are type/layout evidence only, not consumer evidence.

Evidence boundary: no retail Blueprint graphs/packages or other unincluded retail code were inspected. The project guide says gameplay logic is C++, but the absence of a reconstructed consumer is not proof that uninspected packaged retail assets cannot reference this table.

usages.detail: Declares native FName Id and TArray<FName> ImageFileName as BlueprintType UPROPERTY fields; no method in this row struct consumes either value.
The only constructor is empty; it does not initialize a fixed sixteen-element array.
Declaration-only Id_CharacterUniqueImage field: the serialized identifier-level link, with no reconstructed reader.
StartInitialLoading creates DataTable primary-asset loaders from an explicit name list; this table is absent, while CharacterUniqueDataTable1..5 are present at lines 368-372.
Tick resolves explicit loader names into cached table arrays; there is no CharacterUniqueImage resolution or cache assignment.
Records the retail row-struct address and construct thunk for the type; this is registration/layout evidence, not a consumer.
Static layout assertion for ImageFileName at +0x10 (and Id at +0x8 on line 723); verification only.
